The PR branch is behind current main by 29 commits but has 11 isolated reachability files and GitHub currently reports mergeable=true; do not force-rewrite history without a clear reason.
VPN Gate manual workflow measures through volunteer-operated Russian exits; RU egress and ISP/ASN metadata do not attest that a node is a household connection.
VPN Gate tests are manual-only, default 3 servers and hard-capped at 6; no live VPN connection or measurement has yet been run.
VPN Gate tunnel pilot blocks host IPv6 egress and records AAAA DNS answers only; it does not claim IPv6 HTTPS reachability through the tunnel.
VPN Gate exit is accepted only when two independent public IP metadata services agree on exact public IPv4 and country; no consensus is a rejected measurement, not a block result.
Initial VPN Gate sampling inspects up to 24 candidates for RIPEstat origin ASN and prefers distinct ASNs; unknown origin ASN does not count toward distinct-provider coverage.
IP metadata ASN and RIPEstat origin ASN are retained separately; disagreement is an explicit review candidate, not an automatically resolved operator identity.
RIPEstat prefix evidence is accepted only when the CIDR contains the exact IP queried.
VPN Gate manual job has a 120-minute limit; each target's A and AAAA records are fetched by one resolver call, but no IPv6 transport test is claimed.

GitHub workflow_dispatch cannot run from this new feature-branch workflow until the workflow exists on the default branch; a narrow path-and-commit-message-gated one-shot push is used for this draft-branch pilot.

First VPN Gate pilot had a TCP connection but no TLS tunnel; it produced zero RU egress verification and zero service measurements. Its successful Actions conclusion means diagnostic artifacts were uploaded, not that VPN or target reachability succeeded.
AS35807/SkyNet server IP was already mapped as RU by existing prefix 188.242.64.0/18; the server's routed /19 did not produce a new missing-RU IP candidate.

Second pilot #42962715822 had three provider attempts and zero target measurements. The first tunnel reached Initialization Sequence Completed but metadata DNS failed; the other two TCP-connected but did not install the tunnel route. No service access conclusion can be drawn.
Pinned DoH fallback is used only after the VPN tunnel is established; its resolver endpoints are pinned by IP with TLS SNI/certificate validation, avoiding fallback to the host's pre-VPN resolver.
Third pilot run #42964869207 had three TCP/UDP relay attempts without any TUN route; DNS-over-HTTPS was not exercised. The three server IPs were already mapped to RU; no targets were tested.

OpenVPN safe TLS compatibility allowlist is not a broad pass-through: only selected TLS settings and inline trust material are retained; scripts, plugins, external key files and route directives remain excluded.
Final pilot is a single bounded run requesting one verified RU VPN exit from up to six candidates. A green upload step is insufficient; the final measurement gate requires a verified RU exit.

VPN Gate live history so far contains zero service target measurements across first three pilots: first run ended at TLS negotiation; second three attempts had one tunnel initialization but system DNS metadata failure and two no-tunnel relays; third three no-tunnel relays. The final run uses six candidates and expanded TLS profile preservation.

Four live VPN Gate pilot runs resulted in zero completed target measurement rows. Final API snapshot contained three usable profiles across two origin ASNs; all three connection attempts failed to provide a verified RU egress.
All final VPN server endpoint IPs already mapped to existing RU CIDRs. No new CIDR, service accessibility or blocking verdict can be inferred.
DoH fallback and allowlisted TLS compatibility code passed unit tests but was not proven in a live successful tunnel because all final volunteer relay attempts failed before exit verification.
VPN Gate workflow has no scheduled or feature-branch push trigger; workflow_dispatch is manual-only and becomes available when workflow exists on default branch.
The four earlier live VPN Gate pilots used the official CSV API profiles; they did not test the direct VPNObratno-linked IP UDP, UDP, IP TCP and TCP profile variants.
The VPNObratno listing and linked-profile parser have passed deterministic tests, but no live tunnel has yet been established through the newly supported profile variants.
VPNObratno describes its nodes as Russian VPN Gate user-operated servers using Russian ISPs; this does not independently prove that every node is a household broadband connection.
A profile variant is an alternative connection method for one server, not a distinct ISP/provider. Provider diversity is counted only by independently derived origin ASN.
The VPNObratno manual workflow defaults to one verified RU exit and up to six profile attempts; this is a bounded discovery pilot, not a multi-provider completeness claim.
The profile retry budget is bounded across variants and servers. A successful artifact upload is not success unless a confirmed RU exit and target measurement rows are present.
VPNObratno listing/profile downloads are restricted to the exact HTTPS origin; configured proxies and cross-origin redirects are rejected.

VPNObratno documents SSTP and L2TP/IPsec for selected servers, but automated support is not implemented. Do not guess the SSTP port or L2TP endpoint; add them only after machine-readable endpoint discovery and transport-specific fail-closed firewall/route lifecycle validation.
The latest 100-test CI verifies VPNObratno discovery, profile validation and download redirect policy. It does not verify a live VPN tunnel or any target reachability result.

VPNObratno profile discovery now downloads at most 24 profiles per run and interleaves preferred variants across hostnames. Links beyond the cap are reported as omitted; a truncated discovery sample is not complete server/provider coverage.

The current page snapshot showed approximately ten server entries and up to four OpenVPN profile links per entry; the live listing changes over time, so this count is illustrative and each discovery report carries its own actual counts.
The 104-test CI verifies bounded profile downloads and response reads, not live VPN tunnel availability or household/residential access.

VPNObratno discovery response bodies are bounded during streaming: at most 2,000,000 bytes for the listing and 64,000 bytes for each profile; the fetch helper rejects caller limits above 8,000,000 bytes and reads only one byte beyond the resource limit.
